summary: Agent 0.36.0 / router 0.36.0: the agent runs without an NVIDIA GPU (gpu.probe auto|nvidia|none, default auto, ADR-0102), game detection can be switched off (game.enabled, ADR-0103), the game fact's via is 'path' (router maps the old 'pfad'), Home Assistant display names can be English (mqtt.entity_language, unique_id and entity ID unchanged), and the Windows install checks the event-log source in the registry instead of matching error text. B3 (router <-> agent): new fact/heartbeat field gpu_present and the guard state not_applicable from an approved agent. The router takes gpu_present only as a real boolean (heartbeat) or literal false (facts), and memory values only as non-boolean numbers; otherwise the node stays a GPU node or nothing fits. A compromised approved agent could already misreport VRAM, utilisation and guard state (TM-07: telemetry is an assertion of that host); claiming no GPU or not_applicable gives it no capability beyond that: it can attract or repel models for its own node and avoid the require_fresh_status cap, as reporting 'normal' already did. No new route, frame, authentication path or egress. B8 (agent host): install_windows reads HKLM SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\EventLog\Application\<service> read-only in the existing admin install step; service account, ACLs, update and signing paths are unchanged. With gpu.probe auto and no NVIDIA driver at all the GPU guard does not run; without a driver no workload can use the card, so the power-limit protection loses nothing; gpu.probe nvidia keeps the refusal. POST /gpuz stays loopback-only and now answers 409 without a GPU. B9: /health (loopback) gains gpu_probe and gpu_present, MQTT discovery gains constant English names; no secret, host or user data. The fake agent and E2E use loopback and synthetic values only.

tests.evidence: router: facts/heartbeat without GPU values, full-size holdings, no ram_spill, RAM budget and capacity, model_too_large/vram_full, guard not_applicable not capping, older agents unchanged, pfad->path, enabled false; rejected cases: non-numeric memory, non-boolean gpu_present, facts other than false.

tests.command: python test/run_tests.py (through a local lock wrapper that serialises the fixed loopback ports)
tests.evidence: 0 failures, STATE passed; includes the new fake agent with FAKE_GPU=0 (online, gpu_present false, guard not_applicable, no HA problem).

tests.command: all python test/selftest_*.py listed in .github/workflows/ci.yml (Windows, Python 3.12)
tests.evidence: 72 self-tests; selftest_availability needed its fake node to gain capacity_gib/reserve_gib.

tests.evidence: gofmt empty, vet clean on both GOOS, go test ok on Windows (incl. install_windows_test.go).

tests.evidence: PASS (nogpu_test.go, config, mqtt and the other Linux tests).

tests.command: ruff check . ; python router/router.py --check router/config.example.yaml --pure ; python test/check_control_flow.py ; python test/selftest_control_flow.py ; python test/check_pinned_references.py ; python tools/security/lock_requirements.py check

limitations: python test/check_adr_index.py reports one finding on this branch alone: ADR numbers are not consecutive, because ADR-0101 is assigned to a parallel PR that is to be merged first; the index itself was regenerated with --write. CI stays red on that check until ADR-0101 is on main.
The end-to-end suite uses a fake agent; the real agent without a GPU was exercised by Go unit tests (probe none), not on a physical CPU-only machine.
gpu.probe auto on a machine whose NVIDIA driver is missing entirely now starts as a CPU node instead of refusing (documented in ADR-0102).

The router's RAM budget trusts the agent's memory fact like the VRAM fact before (TM-07); on Linux MemAvailable can include page cache of a mapped model, so the budget is an estimate; Ollama's own memory check and memory pressure remain the guard.
The catalog's VRAM measurement (/admin/measure) still needs a GPU; not changed here.
PostgreSQL integrations were not run: no session, memory or storage code changed.
